claims.statement: The control-plane Worker entrypoint dispatches WebSocket upgrades on /sessions/:id/ws to SessionDO (after a SessionIndexStore existence check and 404 for unknown sessions), and sends every other request through handleRequest in router.ts.

The scheduled() handler matches cron expressions exactly: '*' * * * *' runs checkAutofixQueueHealth in waitUntil plus Scheduler.tick() (recovery sweep and overdue automations); '7,37 * * * *' runs the image-build scheduler; '23 * * * *' runs AbandonedDraftSweep. Unknown cron expressions are logged and dropped.

The queue() handler routes by queue name prefix: queues starting with 'open-inspect-github-autofix-' go to handleAutofixQueue (GitHub Autofix, with env.DB injected once), and every other queue is consumed by consumeImageBuildFinalizations (image-build finalization).

The image-build finalization consumer validates each queue message against imageBuildFinalizationJobSchema, acking invalid commands, acking completed work, and retrying busy or failed work with a delay; a failure inside one message never aborts later messages in the batch.

handleRequest rejects a missing env.DB binding once with a 503 before building the request context, so ctx.db is genuinely always present in route handlers and no per-route degraded-mode guards are needed.

handleRequest builds a RequestContext with trace_id from the x-trace-id header (or a fresh UUID), an 8-character request_id, per-request RequestMetrics, an instrumented db handle, and lazy Better Auth runtime getters keyed by the stable env.DB object so cache identity holds across requests.

The router handles OPTIONS preflights with CORS headers, matches the first route by method and regex pattern (route order is significant), and attaches x-request-id, x-trace-id, CORS, and route cacheControl headers to every response.

RouteAuthentication kinds are public, handler-authenticated, web-service, user, user-or-service, sandbox (with a session-id binding), and user-or-service-with-sandbox-fallback; prebuilt policy constants also declare supportedScmProviders, and enforceRoutePrincipal rejects kind mismatches (401 for web-service, 403 for user routes).

Sandbox-auth routes derive the session id from the path match and verify the bearer token with the session's Durable Object via POST /internal/verify-sandbox-token; a DO outage or error maps to 503 'Sandbox authentication unavailable'. On routes with sandbox fallback, a request with no recognized credential is tried as a sandbox-token call only when the authentication failed with failedScheme 'none'.

authenticate() resolves every non-public, non-sandbox request to a typed Principal: a sig1 service signature verified against the per-service secret, optionally exchanged through a Better Auth session into a user principal when the request rides the web channel and the route requires webService 'user'; anything else is rejected as failedScheme 'none'.

Service-signature verification buffers and hashes the body up to SERVICE_REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES (16 MiB), validates the sig1 header before buffering, logs nonce reuse best-effort in-isolate, and rejects unknown services or missing per-service secrets with a 500 'not configured' response — never a downgrade.

There are exactly three Principal kinds — user (carrying userId), service (carrying an asserted actor restricted by ASSERTION_RIGHTS per service name), and sandbox (carrying only sessionId) — and the shapes make illegal states unrepresentable: only service principals can carry asserted actors.

enforceImplementedScmProvider resolves the deployment's SCM provider once (memoized on the env value) and returns 501 for routes whose supportedScmProviders exclude it, and 500 for a permanently broken provider configuration.

Handler exceptions are centralized: HttpError maps to error(message, status), any other throw is logged with D1 metrics and returned as a 500, and every request emits structured auth.principal and http.request log lines with request_id, trace_id, duration_ms, and outcome.

instrumentD1 wraps a SqlDatabase so every statement terminal method (run, first, all) and batch records wall-clock query_ms, engine-reported d1_server_ms, and rows read/written into the per-request RequestMetrics collector, whose summary spreads into the http.request wide event as d1_query_count, d1_total_ms, d1_server_total_ms, d1_rows_read, and d1_rows_written.

instrumented statements store the original via the ORIGINAL_STMT symbol and batch() unwraps them before execution because a database can execute only its own prepared statements; bind() chains return newly instrumented statements so chained queries stay timed.

The SqlDatabase port is the engine-neutral SQL surface for all src/db stores: meta.changes is required because ~38 call sites gate correctness on it (CAS conflict detection, guarded lifecycle transitions, upsert detection), and batch() must be atomic with positional 1:1 result mapping. D1Database satisfies the port structurally with no runtime wrapper.

An ESLint rule (no-restricted-syntax on MemberExpression property 'DB') forbids reading env.DB anywhere except composition roots — router.ts, the index.ts crons, the queue consumers, and the SessionDO constructor — so route handlers use ctx.db and all queries are timed. The session DO's synchronous SqlStorage is intentionally not covered by the SqlDatabase port.

SessionDO is a thin Cloudflare platform adapter: it reads env.DB once in its constructor, builds the full session runtime lazily on first touch (initSchema on the embedded SqlStorage, then createSessionRuntime), publishes the runtime only after construction succeeds so a throw leaves the activation retriable, and forwards fetch/webSocketMessage/webSocketClose/webSocketError/alarm to the platform-neutral SessionServer.

Session InternalPaths constants shared between the router and SessionDO (init, prompt, stop, messages, events, verify-sandbox-token, ws-token, expire-draft, scm-credentials, and more) prevent path drift; createSessionRuntimeClient resolves SESSION.idFromName(sessionId) and forwards x-trace-id/x-request-id headers to the DO.
sessionRoute() wrappers inject ctx.sessionRuntime into route handlers, so most session routes are thin proxies performing D1-side enforcement and forwarding to the session Durable Object.

Session creation is a two-step flow: handleCreateSession resolves identity, SCM repository access, model, integration settings, managed skills, and provider auth entirely against D1, then initializeSession writes the 'created' row to the D1 index BEFORE posting /internal/init to the SessionDO; a failed or non-2xx DO init triggers best-effort compensation marking the D1 row 'failed' so no phantom created session appears in listings.

BackgroundTasks is the narrow capability for deferring work: the Cloudflare adapter calls ExecutionContext.waitUntil on the pending promise, absorbs synchronous throws from the task factory exactly like rejections, and logs every failure as background_task.failed.

The GitHub automation event webhook is a user-or-service route that validates the normalized envelope, submits pull-request lifecycle tracking off the request path (additive work whose failure never affects automation matching), then forwards the event to the scheduler.

The per-minute Scheduler.tick caps work for backpressure: MAX_PER_TICK = 25 automations, TICK_CHILD_LAUNCH_BUDGET = 50 child launches (each costs about eight subrequests), ORPHAN_THRESHOLD_MS = 5 minutes for starting-run recovery, and DEFAULT_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 90 minutes for timed-out runs; work left overdue is picked up next tick.

AbandonedDraftSweep runs on its own cron '23 * * * *' (not the per-minute tick, to avoid sharing the tick's subrequest budget) and archives sessions still in 'created' after ABANDONED_DRAFT_TTL_MS = 8 hours by asking each session DO to retire itself, capped at 50 candidates per sweep with a 10 s per-request timeout; expiry outcomes are zod-validated at the boundary.

The image-build scheduler cron '7,37 * * * *' runs republish-recoverable-finalizations, stale-build marking, provider session cleanup, SCM scope reconciliation, and artifact reaping; each phase catches and logs failures independently.

checkAutofixQueueHealth (per-minute tick, waitUntil) inspects AUTOFIX_QUEUE and AUTOFIX_DLQ metrics — read-only bindings — and logs error events when the primary backlog exceeds 25 messages, the oldest primary message exceeds 5 minutes, or the dead-letter queue holds anything.

Production control-plane configuration is Terraform-generated (terraform/environments/production/workers-control-plane.tf plus the cloudflare-worker module); wrangler.jsonc is test-only config. There is no checked-in production wrangler.toml. Durable Object class creation requires a two-phase deploy: enable_durable_object_bindings = false first, then true; class deletion has a plan-time precondition demanding bindings stay enabled.

The Worker is deployed through the 3-resource pattern (cloudflare_worker, cloudflare_worker_version with a built index.js bundle, cloudflare_workers_deployment at 100%) with observability enabled at head sampling rate 1; cron triggers ['* * * * *', '7,37 * * * *', '23 * * * *'] must stay in sync with scheduler constants.

GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY must be PKCS#8 format for Cloudflare Workers (an RSA private key in BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY form fails Web Crypto import); Terraform wires it as a secret binding together with GITHUB_APP_ID and GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID.

The image-build finalization queue consumer is Terraform-configured with batch_size 1, max_wait_time_ms 1000, max_concurrency 5, max_retries 12, retry_delay 15, and a dead-letter queue; the control-plane worker holds producer bindings for IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_QUEUE and (when the GitHub bot is enabled) AUTOFIX_QUEUE/AUTOFIX_DLQ for read-only metrics.

Secrets-at-rest encryption keys (TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY) are validated eagerly as strict base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes for AES-256; a missing or malformed key fails at first touch rather than downgrading cipher strength or falling back to plaintext.

Sandbox lifecycle durations are millisecond environment variables with _MS suffixes: SANDBOX_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 600000 (10 minutes) and EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 5400000 (90 minutes); sandbox providers are selected via SANDBOX_PROVIDER (modal, daytona, vercel, opencomputer, or e2b).
Queue metrics binding is deliberately read-only: Autofix production consumption remains owned by the GitHub bot worker, while the control plane checks queue health on the per-minute tick.
